questions.text:
Waka Wonders has a target profit of $60,000 for the year.

(i) Calculate the number of toys that must be sold to achieve this target profit.
(ii) If maximum production capacity is 6,000 toys per year, calculate the margin of safety at this capacity.
(iii) What is the minimum selling price per toy (to the nearest dollar) needed to achieve the target profit at a sales volume of 5,500 toys?
questions.markingGuide: Show calculations with proper cost and revenue analysis, noting capacity constraint.

questions.text:
Waka Wonders is considering two production options. The table above shows the details of each option.

For each option, calculate the break-even point and the profit at an estimated demand of 5,500 toys. Recommend which option Waka Wonders should choose and justify your answer.
questions.markingGuide: Calculate and interpret margin of safety for both options in business context.

questions.text: Based on your CVP analysis, recommend which option Waka Wonders should choose. In your answer, consider: the profit impact, the risk profile (margin of safety), quality control implications, and the strategic importance of keeping the handcrafted identity. Justify your recommendation with quantitative evidence.
questions.expectedAnswer: Option B generates significantly more profit ($47,000 vs $23,000) and has a larger margin of safety (1,807 toys vs 958 toys). However, outsourcing means losing direct control over the handcrafted quality that defines the brand. Risks: dependency on one workshop, potential inconsistency, loss of the 'handmade in Rotorua' story. Recommendation: Option A is strategically better despite lower profit, because the handcrafted identity is central to the premium price. The CNC equipment still allows 'handcrafted' claims while improving consistency. The $24,000 profit difference may be offset by the brand premium that justifies the $45 price point.
questions.markingGuide: Justify recommendations with quantitative CVP analysis and qualitative strategic considerations.
